description: Sabotage manifest for windows-platform-probes. Each entry is a defect that was actually run by hand while building M3; the manifest exists so those one-off verifications stop being discarded. See CHECKLIST.md M2.14.1. Run with --all-features because the corpus target, tests/a_real_report_agrees_with_itself.rs, requires oracle-in-renderer: with default features it is not built, so an entry only that target catches -- a wrong arm in its codes_for, for one -- would be scored as surviving.

sabotages.name: row drops the packages field
sabotages.why: A field silently vanishes from every mined row. This is the defect that was MEASURED to leave the whole suite green before MEASURED_ROW_KEYS existed, so this entry is the regression test for the key-set contract itself.

sabotages.name: row writer emits a leading separator
sabotages.why: Produces a row that is bracket-balanced but not valid JSON, so a consumer's parser rejects it. The oracle's old `balanced` check counted depth and passed exactly this; `malformation` must not.

sabotages.name: row writer does not escape quotes
sabotages.why: A quote in a caller's `io::Error` ends the JSON string early and lets the rest of the message forge keys in the mined row. `write_escaped` is the whole of the injection fix.

sabotages.name: the row's key reader uses a parsed map
sabotages.why: The obvious simplification, and it is wrong twice over: a serde_json::Map SORTS its names and silently keeps the LAST of a repeated key -- so this loses the row's key ORDER, which is part of the contract MEASURED_ROW_KEYS states, and it deletes the evidence for RowDefect::RepeatedKey, the one malformation that survives a consumer's parse. This entry exists so that the reason the visitor is not a map cannot be forgotten.
find: let Ok(names) = serde::Deserializer::deserialize_map(&mut reader, TopLevelNames) else {

sabotages.name: cross_check forgets the changed bracket
sabotages.why: THE entry this crate's invariant module exists for. Deleting the push empties the list, so `verdict()` -- a pure function of the lists -- legitimately returns `agree` beside an observation whose bracket did not hold. Any rule reading the LISTS is blind to this by construction; only a rule reading the OBSERVATION catches it.

sabotages.name: a blocking state with no perturbation
sabotages.why: An untested blocking state. Adds rather than deletes, deliberately: a hand-written `ALL` was measured to let exactly this through while all ten invariant tests stayed green. Declared refused-by-build since M4.1 put this manifest on --all-features: the corpus target's `codes_for` matches every state exhaustively, so a state with no row code no longer compiles, which is the stronger rung. The perturbation guard this entry used to reach is sabotaged by the entry below instead.
find: BracketNotHeld => "the bracket did not establish that the machine held still",
replace: BracketNotHeld => "the bracket did not establish that the machine held still",
/// A state added by a sabotage, with no perturbation behind it.

sabotages.name: a blocking state loses its perturbation
sabotages.why: The deletion twin of the entry above, and since --all-features the one that reaches every_blocking_state_has_a_perturbation: the state still exists, so everything compiles, and only the comparison against BlockingState::ALL notices that nothing shows it fires.

sabotages.name: prose reworded to carry the same fact
sabotages.why: THE CONTROL, and it encodes this component's central decision as a measurement rather than as prose: the row is the machine contract and the prose is for a reader, so no test may derive a MACHINE-CONTRACT requirement from the wording. Note the narrowness -- tests may and do assert prose (about 35 of them read report text with contains), because the human report is a deliverable and its content is worth covering. What none of them may do is parse the prose, or pin a sentence the row is separately responsible for. So this entry rewords a line no test asserts, and if it is ever reported as caught, the question to ask is WHICH test caught it: one that reads the wording to learn something the row already publishes is the defect, and one that simply covers this sentence means the entry needs a different sentence.
find: let _ = writeln!(out, "cache boundary divides this machine.");
replace: let _ = writeln!(out, "cache boundary splits this machine.");

sabotages.name: blocking_states relaxes the processor guard
sabotages.why: The guard says a machine with processors and no packages is a finding; relaxing it to >= makes a topology that reported NOTHING a finding too, accusing a synthetic observation of hiding packages it never claimed. This condition exists TWICE on purpose -- cross_check has its own copy, and blocking_states must recompute rather than read cross_check's output, or it restates verdict() and goes blind to a deleted push site. Independence is the design; agreement is the property. A mutation sweep found the property untested: the test that names this boundary asserts on cross_check, so it covered only the other copy, and this mutation survived five review rounds across four models. Kept here so the pairing is re-run rather than re-discovered.

sabotages.name: request_cost: the grafted row is given a path that is not grafted
sabotages.why: The row is named for what the build does with its path. A relative sample that stopped being relative would leave build_request_grafted timing a path kept as given under the wrong name, and nothing in the report would say so; the probe checks its own samples, and that check fails the run.

sabotages.name: request_cost: the long kept row is given a path that would be grafted
sabotages.why: The other direction: a sample meant to be kept as given that is in fact grafted would leave build_request_kept_long timing the graft under the name of the other case.

sabotages.name: request_cost: the share_handle row is measured and not recorded
sabotages.why: M7.1: the row that times what a request now does with a handle would silently leave the report and its NDJSON line, which the census of every label exists to refuse.

sabotages.name: request_cost control: the shared handle is cloned through the trait path
sabotages.why: A control: the same clone spelled another way, which no test can tell apart.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: the median ignores the repetitions the run was given
sabotages.why: A run asked for more repetitions would report the default's median while its settings line said otherwise -- the settings would be decoration.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: each pass performs the default pushes whatever the run was given
sabotages.why: The timed passes would push the default count while the divisor used the given one, so every per-operation figure would be off by their ratio. The timer and the divisor read one value so that this cannot happen.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: --producers is accepted and dropped
sabotages.why: The flag would parse and validate and then change nothing, so a run asked for other producer counts would silently measure the defaults.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: every sampling claims to be the default
sabotages.why: A report sampled other than the defaults would say it was the published configuration -- the one confusion the settings line exists to prevent.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: every iteration multiplier claims to be the default
sabotages.why: The cost probes' settings line would call a scaled run the default, so its figures would pass for the published ones.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: a refused command line exits as a success
sabotages.why: A script that mistyped a flag would read status 0 and an empty stdout as a run that measured nothing.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling: the cost probe's NDJSON line drops the multiplier
sabotages.why: A machine reader would see a scaled run's figures with nothing saying they were not the default's.

sabotages.name: M4.2 sampling control: the warmup pass is discarded another way
sabotages.why: A control: the untimed pass still runs with the same arguments and its result is still thrown away, which no test can tell apart.

sabotages.name: M4.1: cross_check forgets overlapping walk relations
sabotages.why: One of the eleven push sites blocking_states did not model before M4.1. Deleting it empties the list, so the verdict reaches agree beside an observation that still holds the overlap; only a rule reading the observation sees it.

sabotages.name: M4.1: cross_check forgets a cache level with no partitions
sabotages.why: The same class through a condition computed from the caches rather than read from a count, which is the case the old exclusion argument mistook for the cross-check's own arithmetic.

sabotages.name: M4.1: cross_check forgets a described relation
sabotages.why: Deleting this push does NOT reach agree: a described relation also files counts_include_unparsed_relations under not_compared, so the verdict stays incomplete and the invariant module has nothing to say. What is lost is the code a survey groups by. Two tests see that: a_relation_a_caller_described_is_not_a_measurement, which fails first and so is the one a sweep's transcript names, and the corpus's every_state_that_blocks_agreement_reaches_the_row, confirmed by running the corpus target alone against this patch.

sabotages.name: M4.1: blocking_states reads only the core half of an empty relation
sabotages.why: The perturbation table reaches this state through the core field alone, so dropping the package half passes every test that iterates the table. A package covering no processors would then leave cross_check free to lose its push unnoticed.

sabotages.name: M4.1: blocking_states drops the measured guard on absent counts
sabotages.why: cross_check files measured_but_counts_absent only for a measured topology. Without the guard the state fires for an unmeasured one too, and the per-state publication rule would demand a code the row never emits for it.

sabotages.name: M4.1: a state answers the wrong code
sabotages.why: The schema between states and row codes is written by hand because neither side can derive it. A wrong arm leaves described_relations answered by no state, which the census test exists to refuse.

sabotages.name: M4.1 control: a count compared with != rather than >
sabotages.why: A control: for a usize the two comparisons agree on every value, so no test can tell them apart.

sabotages.name: M2.17: coherence is checked only when the bracket held
sabotages.why: A check selected by two dimensions at once: an unheld bracket hides a coherence disagreement, so the row publishes no enumerations_disagreed for an observation in that blocking state. The bracket once suppressed every parse check above it by an early return, so this is a defect this code has shipped. No hand-written shape varies the bracket and the coherence together; the generated cross product does.

sabotages.name: M2.17: a crossed value changes nothing
sabotages.why: A dimension value that changes nothing collapses every combination it is in onto the one beside it: the product keeps its length and its names while reaching a third fewer states, and nothing that renders the shapes can tell. The independence test exists to refuse it.

sabotages.name: M2.17 control: a crossed value renamed
sabotages.why: A control: the name is only how a failing shape is reported, so renaming one changes no state the corpus reaches.

sabotages.name: M8.1: the queue probe stops emitting its row
sabotages.why: The census runs this probe rather than reading its sources, so whether its row exists is decided by its output. Before M8.1 the census grepped for the literal "reason":"x-probe, which a row built with Row::new never contains; since M8.2 the probe emits exactly such a row, and deleting it must change the census's set.

sabotages.name: M8.2: the row publishes per-operation figures as elapsed times
sabotages.why: The elapsed fields are recovered by multiplying back by the run's total pushes; publishing the per-operation figure under an elapsed name is the plausible slip.
find: Value::from((per_op * total as f64).round() as usize)

sabotages.name: M8.2: the recovered elapsed time is truncated instead of rounded
sabotages.why: Dividing by the pushes and multiplying back can land a hair below the whole nanosecond it started from; truncation then publishes one nanosecond less than the pass took.
find: Value::from((per_op * total as f64).round() as usize)
replace: Value::from((per_op * total as f64) as usize)

sabotages.name: M8.2: the fastest and slowest passes trade places
sabotages.why: Every test with one repetition has the three passes equal, so only distinct passes can tell the fields apart.

sabotages.name: M8.2: a configuration that did not measure publishes zero
sabotages.why: Zero reads as an immeasurably fast pass; null says there was none.

sabotages.name: M8.2 control: the row names its build before its architecture
sabotages.why: A control: a row is read by key, so the order its keys are written in is not something the tests claim.

sabotages.name: M8.3: the peer-index probe stops emitting its row
sabotages.why: The census runs the probe, so a measured run that prints no row changes the set it reports.

sabotages.name: M8.3: the row publishes the per-item figure as the elapsed time
sabotages.why: The elapsed field is recovered by multiplying back by the items; publishing the per-item cost under an elapsed name is the plausible slip.
find: Value::from((run.nanos_per_item * ITEMS as f64).round() as usize)

sabotages.name: M8.3: the recovered elapsed time is truncated instead of rounded
sabotages.why: Dividing by the items and multiplying back can land a hair below the whole nanosecond it started from; truncation then publishes one nanosecond less than the pass took.
find: Value::from((run.nanos_per_item * ITEMS as f64).round() as usize)
replace: Value::from((run.nanos_per_item * ITEMS as f64) as usize)

sabotages.name: M8.3: the consumer and producer read counts trade places
sabotages.why: The two counts carry the finding -- which side's reads the technique removed -- and nothing about their types tells them apart.

sabotages.name: M8.3: the shipping queue publishes its floor as counted reads
sabotages.why: The shipping queue has no counter; its read fields hold ITEMS as a floor, and publishing that puts a constant under a name that says it was counted.

sabotages.name: M8.3: the strategies follow a different fixed order
sabotages.why: The order is part of what the row states; a reader comparing two runs by position must find the same strategy in the same place.

sabotages.name: M8.3: a measured row omits the declined field
sabotages.why: Without it a reader can tell a measured row from a declined one only by which other fields happen to exist.

sabotages.name: M8.3: a declined row loses the reason
sabotages.why: A declined row that says null for why is indistinguishable from a measured one in that field.

sabotages.name: M8.3 control: the row names its build before its architecture
sabotages.why: A control: a row is read by key, so the order its keys are written in is not something the tests claim.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the core-affinity probe stops emitting its row
sabotages.why: The census runs the probe, so a measured run that prints no row changes the set it reports.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the row publishes the per-item figure as the elapsed time
sabotages.why: The raw elapsed time now travels on the measurement; publishing the derived per-item cost under an elapsed name is the plausible slip.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the consumer and producer read counts trade places
sabotages.why: Nothing about their types tells the two counts apart.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the requested and achieved memory nodes trade places
sabotages.why: A row whose request and result disagree did not measure the placement it names; swapping them reports the redirect backwards.

sabotages.name: M8.4: an absent cache domain is published as not observed
sabotages.why: The prose keeps 'no level partitions the machine' and 'this processor was left out of the level' apart; conflating them states a negative where nothing was observed, or the reverse.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the reading after the run is published as the measured one
sabotages.why: The three readings are what a reader compares to know which machine the rows belong to; publishing one twice hides a change.

sabotages.name: M8.4: the by-class list publishes the placement rows
sabotages.why: Each list is a different selection of pairs; filling one from another is a row that names the wrong question.

sabotages.name: M8.4: a declined row loses the reason
sabotages.why: A declined row that says null for why is indistinguishable from a measured one in that field.

sabotages.name: M8.4 control: the row names its build before its architecture
sabotages.why: A control: a row is read by key, so the order its keys are written in is not something the tests claim.

sabotages.name: M8.5: the pool-growth probe stops emitting its row
sabotages.why: The census runs the probe, so a run that prints no row changes the set it reports.

sabotages.name: M8.5: the runs-long flag is not taken from the run
sabotages.why: Two runs share a maximum and a submission count and differ only in this flag; without it their rows are indistinguishable but for the name.

sabotages.name: M8.5: the two observed counts trade places
sabotages.why: Callbacks started and threads used are equal on a healthy run, which is exactly why a swap would go unseen on one.

sabotages.name: M8.5: whether the raise took effect is inverted
sabotages.why: The elapsed time means the raise's delay or the settle window according to this flag alone.

sabotages.name: M8.5: the raise's elapsed time is published in microseconds
sabotages.why: The arrivals are microseconds and the raise is nanoseconds; carrying the wrong unit under the `_ns` name is the plausible slip.

sabotages.name: M8.5: a yes-or-no renders backwards
sabotages.why: Every boolean any row publishes goes through this one arm.

sabotages.name: M8.5 control: the row names its build before its architecture
sabotages.why: A control: a row is read by key, so the order its keys are written in is not something the tests claim.

sabotages.name: M8.6: the long-path probes stop emitting their row
sabotages.why: Both binaries share this renderer, so the census sees two probes lose their row at once.

sabotages.name: M8.6: the row claims the manifest whatever the binary declares
sabotages.why: The finding is the difference between the two binaries; a row that does not say which one it came from cannot be paired.

sabotages.name: M8.6: an attempt that opened publishes the error it never read
sabotages.why: The apparatus leaves the error at zero on success without calling GetLastError; publishing it reads as a code that was observed.

sabotages.name: M8.6: a registry value never read is published as off
sabotages.why: The module's own note records this exact defect in the prose: a refused run reporting the machine half absent on a host where it is set.

sabotages.name: M8.6: a refused run loses the reason
sabotages.why: When the apparatus fails the attempts say nothing about the machine, and this field is the only thing that says so.

sabotages.name: M8.6: two shapes trade record names
sabotages.why: The two shapes that do not survive verbatim parsing are the hypothesis; swapping their names attributes each one's result to the other.

sabotages.name: M8.6 control: the row names its build before its architecture
sabotages.why: A control: a row is read by key, so the order its keys are written in is not something the tests claim.

sabotages.name: M8.1 control: the short run takes two pushes fewer
sabotages.why: A control: how much a short run measures is incidental to which lines its report carries.

sabotages.name: M4.8: the capture script ignores the build
sabotages.why: Runs of two builds would agree on every other attribution line and have their medians combined as though one procedure produced both -- the defect M4.8 exists to refuse.

sabotages.name: M4.8: the queue report stops naming its build
sabotages.why: A report without the line would read as unstamped, which the capture scripts accept beside other unstamped runs -- so the build check would silently stop applying to new captures.

sabotages.name: M4.8: the build script stops stamping this crate
sabotages.why: The identity is read with env!, so a build script that stamps nothing cannot produce a binary that reports a made-up identity: the compiler refuses it. Kept to show that rung holds.

sabotages.name: M4.8 control: the script test's scratch directory renamed
sabotages.why: A control: the directory's name is incidental to what the scripts are given.

sabotages.name: M4.4: every run takes the sequential order
sabotages.why: The default would be back to back again while the report said interleaved, so the control would be measured apart under a line claiming it was not.

sabotages.name: M4.4: interleaved rounds stop rotating
sabotages.why: Without the rotation the same configuration is always measured first in a round, so position in the round can align with whatever the first pass after the previous round's last absorbs. The balance the item asked for is the rotation.

sabotages.name: M4.4: --order is accepted and dropped
sabotages.why: A run asked for the sequential order would measure interleaved while the command line said otherwise, and the published figures could not be retaken.

sabotages.name: M4.4: the sequential order is no longer the published one
sabotages.why: Swapping two configurations changes no row and no table, so only the test pinning the list notices -- and without it --order sequential would quietly stop retaking the figures it exists to retake.

sabotages.name: M4.4: the report omits the order
sabotages.why: The order is a capture parameter: figures taken interleaved and back to back are measurements of different procedures, and a captured report that does not say which cannot be compared with anything.

sabotages.name: M4.4 control: the configuration count read another way
sabotages.why: A control: the same count by iteration, which no test can tell apart.
